authority.summary: No owner, no admin and no upgrade path: the ABI has no function that could add one. The program, the page, the image and the words are four immutable pointers, set at construction and checked against commitments there. One write changes the work's state, saveMind, and only the token's holder may send it; an approved operator cannot, because the holder check is ownerOf itself. The standard's writes move the token and nothing else.

authority.summary: Two writes, both spent. mint could be called by the minter until the lock, once per id, with that id's row of the table; lock could be called once, only after all sixty-four existed, and it set the minter to the zero address. Since then nothing an address can change remains, and the base program, the image and the renderer were immutable from construction.

recipes.title: Read a mind
recipes.text: The head brain of the canary, 834 bytes, from any node.

recipes.title: Pull a program out and run it off the chain
recipes.text: Any Chamber token's program, stamped with the block you pulled it at. Save the hex as a file and it is an ordinary C64 program; a browser emulator will boot it.

recipes.title: Train a brain without owning a token
recipes.text: The same replay the contract uses to judge a save, as a free call: hand it any admissible 834-byte parent and any lesson stream, get the child back.

recipes.title: Pin a revision for ever
recipes.text: Every revision's brain is its own data contract. Read the record, take the blob's address, and read the bytes straight from it - skipping the first byte, which is a STOP.
recipes.code:
cast call 0x6f54E1aAE0E9A679A52e5E733645cB11e0cE6127 'revision(uint256,uint32)' 1 3 --rpc-url $RPC   # the first word is the brain blob's address
cast code $BLOB --rpc-url $RPC   # 0x00 then the 834 bytes
